pr_body:
### Description

Yarn 4 changed how patches can get encoded in the lockfile and `resolutions` field in the root `package.json`. Primarily the changes are with direct dependencies that are patched. These now will appear in the `package.json` and the workspace's `dependency`map in the lockfile entry.

This PR alters our behavior to now properly handle these direct dependencies.

Closes #6450

### Testing Instructions

Added new unit tests with Yarn 4 fixtures. Tested out pruning manually by creating a test repo with direct and indirect patches:

#### Setup
```
npx create-turbo@latest yarn4 yarn
cd yarn4
echo "nodeLinker: node-modules" >> .yarnrc.yml
yarn set version 4
cd apps/docs
yarn add is-odd
yarn patch is-odd
# follow patch commands to patch is-odd
cd ../web
yarn add is-even
cd ../..
```

#### Testing
Test that pruning both `web` and `docs` prune properly:
```
[0 olszewski@chriss-mbp] /tmp/yarn4 $ turbo_dev prune web
Generating pruned monorepo for web in /private/tmp/yarn4/out
 - Added @repo/eslint-config
 - Added @repo/typescript-config
 - Added @repo/ui
 - Added web
[0 olszewski@chriss-mbp] /tmp/yarn4 $ cd out 
[0 olszewski@chriss-mbp] /tmp/yarn4/out $ yarn install --immutable
```



Closes TURBO-2022

issue_context.title: [turborepo] Yarn v4 patch causes `turbo prune` to panic, no locator found
issue_context.body:
### What version of Turborepo are you using?

1.10.16

### What package manager are you using / does the bug impact?

Yarn v2/v3 (node_modules linker only)

### What operating system are you using?

Mac

### Describe the Bug

```txt
yarn turbo prune --scope MobileApp
Generating pruned monorepo for MobileApp in /Users/username/projectname
 - Added @project/client-shared
 - Added @project/core
 - Added @project/graphql
 - Added @project/openapi
 - Added @project/tsconfig
 - Added @project/types
 - Added MobileApp
 - Added eslint-config-project
thread 'main' panicked at crates/turborepo-lockfiles/src/berry/mod.rs:456:44:
No locator found for @openapi-codegen/typescript@npm:^6.2.0
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

Where I have the following (simplified) `package.json`:

root:

```json
{
  "packageManager": "yarn@4.0.2",
  "resolutions": {
    "@openapi-codegen/typescript@^6.2.0": "patch:@openapi-codegen/typescript@npm%3A6.2.0#./.yarn/patches/@openapi-codegen-typescript-npm-6.2.0-c197461d23.patch"
  }
}
```

`@project/openapi`

```json
{
  "name": "@project/openapi",
  "devDependencies": {
    "@openapi-codegen/typescript": "^6.2.0"
  }
}
```

review_comments: Make this private to ensure external callers go through the trait and don't call this directly.

This test asserted some buggy behavior as it identified `lodash` as being an extension when it was really a user patch.

What we truly care about is that this `lodash` package gets included in the closure. This is asserted by the `test_closure_with_patch` test.

This is an oopsie from 6 months ago where we ended up having duplicate definitions for `subgraph` one on `BerryLockfile` and one on the `Lockfile` implementation. This unifies them by forwarding the trait implementation to the type one.
For my own understanding, do we hash local patches for the purposes for cache invalidation?

At the moment no, but that is something we probably should do. Doing it properly will require a little bit of work to make it performant as currently we require building a whole pruned lockfile in order to know what patches affect a set of packages.

Currently the best solution would be to include `.yarn/patches` in the `globalDependencies`.
